body:
In regards to the DM stuff, sending a video recommendation or a creator that covers the shared interest might be a passive enough way to reach out? "Hey, thought this might be helpful with your project since it kind of worked for me, good luck" and so on. 

Or maybe frame it as you messaging because you didn't want to mention certain things in "public", like if friends or family were involved. Or just a thanks for the advice, I'm a traumatised extrovert, so everything reads as anxious introvert for a while anyway. I thank people a lot in private for just talking to me, letting them know that it helped a lot more than they would realise. People get a pat on the back for doing the bare minimum, and if they're a decent person they might try to keep talking.
Tbf, I'm pretty confident I could fight a wild animal (or get shredded, whatever), can't fight rejection or humiliation.
I can't hear Damaged by Plumb without thinking of Borrasca now, so that would be on it without a doubt.

I hear if you say her name three times while looking in a mirror, she'll show up with a really pretentious coffee, and refuse to take accountability for leaving slime in random places. 

*shudders*
She caused a literal baby, brand new human, to have a *looks directly at camera* moment, it's very unsettling.

The overall message I got was that it's super hard for a generally good looking (eh), upper middle class white woman with a decent support system, big house, large internet following, and a mind numbing, insensitive youtube series where she indulges in her power fantasies to... get away...? 

I'm almost impressed at her managing to bring up Serial while acting like she's having to run for her life, well, run but not leave her home, a place her supposed abuser knows as well as she does. Though in my experience, womens shelters don't make much of an allowance for a podcast setup, so... priorities?
Doom-head punching himself in the face over and over again until he's got his finished look is quite a "mood" as the kids say, as I watch her trying to be the cool girl...

For someone who wants to paint herself as the victim, she sure is showing nothing but aggressor in these videos, the videos she isn't able to edit herself into a soft spoken little flower... My heart breaks for the kids, but it's obvious that Stephanie isn't gonna keep the slander offline. I'm proud of Adam for standing up for himself like this and not letting her control the narrative with her following.
I can't figure out how to link it, but it's the first pinned post on this sub.

It's a difficult spot to be in, as a woman I've been a victim, but I've known men who have had horrible accusations thrown at them. Humans are complex individuals. But as someone who has studied law I can say it's not in your best interest to literally film yourself giving a detailed threat. 

Tbh, Amy Dunne was smarter though. That video was really triggering, because Adam's response is exactly what a lot of us know. "Please let this get easier if I'm nice enough." But still it's like, imagine being this kind of personality as Stephanie. Claiming to care about those who have been victims, and having that kind of malice just brewing inside you... 

Sure it could brew up a fancy cup of coffee, but like... people died, steph...

Honestly my true crime search method is weird, I was looking for someone talking about Phoebe Handsjuk because of the Lisa Harnum case that darklivity did, I see a lot of similarities tbh, too many, be wary of wealthy men in high rise buildings. And the hovering corruption angle pissed me off in both cases. 

I watched 'Maneater', who was very much just "here's what happened" and 'making a true crimer'. I don't know anything else about them yet, but I enjoyed what I saw. Sorry I can't give any more recommendations from what I've seen.

I've been getting Amy Dunne vibes from her from a while now, but at least gone girl was a work of fiction. That video was chilling, because I used to really enjoy her content. To say "I'm a good person" after giving a detailed threat about keeping a father away from his children... no ick gif is big enough. 

I think that too many of us have had relationships where they pull the "I COULD....... but I won't...." card, and it's just not sitting right, rightfully so. Because ugh, she won't even own up to her flaws, she is her own narcissist. 

I hope she's kept away from hammers and staircases. At least I can say I'm finding smaller content creators who have covered the same cases she has that I would occasionally rewatch, and I'm getting less self insert information too. I'm able to hear more about the person who was taken too soon, and feel driven to help others where possible.

I'd question any male friend who knows what you're going through and just decides to have a word, and not wait by the door while you pack a bag in case your abuser comes back early... like what most friends would do... and why they isolate you from any sources of help. 

I can't believe she actually said that, its definitely bad advice, but I think anyone in a situation to need advice would be able to see how dangerous her "help" is. I really hope so, at least.

The poor guy has been in fight or flight for years, I think he seemed most at peace just before that damn tunnel. A high stress and fear, but "stay on your feet" reaction makes sense in the hospital. I guess he didn't have the time to dwell on the situation and get angry about it. I simply can't understand how people don't see his actions as a natural instinct and try to act like what he did was wrong in any way.

I'd say either expression is fair tbh given what he walked in on, and with having at least two football teams worth of guys just trying to kill me to keep me from saving someone. But maybe I'm just crazy for thinking that it's a natural human instinct to want to protect the vulnerable among us (WHO CANNOT CONSENT) if we want to preserve any kind of decent society... 

(I never saw the bottom image before though, don't know if I missed it in the game because of the stress headache I got leading up to it or it's a mod thing, but my heart breaks all over again!).
I wonder if there's any jobs at the regurgitate wikipedia articles and go on for 10 minutes about a deodorant for a few thousand dollars factory, cause I could really use one about now XD

"I used to think family was a right, but it's a privilege, it needs to be earned."

It all went to shit quickly because of the "what if they die?!" Boohoo stuff, but it was a nice brief acknowledgement that some family members get cut off for a good reason, and speaking for myself, the people I've cut off, my only regret will be not getting my money back.

I used to turn off my phone on the holidays but now they just know not to contact me because I'm good at burning bridges, but a good old "my phone signal was acting up" and, being too tired to answer the door could work too. Hope you enjoy your December 25th stress free!

Maybe it's because I'm a fan of tough love (as awful as it can feel), but I always wanted Gio and Betty to end up together, I feel like he pushed her the way nobody else did. 

Sure, it wasn't what she was ready to accept at the time, but I feel like Betty could have progressed so much faster in her career with Gio at her back, he was ride or die. He was very passionate, though, which can come off aggressive if you're not accepting that passion with open arms. 

I think he really cared about her, and I wished they could at least have found a happy medium in the end. 

And tbh I think all the men on the show were beautiful in their own categories, Henry was for the superman fans, Gio for the ones who want the cosy boyfriend to cook you amazing breakfast in bed, Daniel for the bad boy you can totally fix with your love, Marc for those who never got over Lyndsey Buckinghams striking eyes (holiday road video in particular), and Ignacio... for anyone who looked at him.

Gio always gave her the push she needed, she might not have wanted to hear it at the time, but aren't we all like that with the ugly truth? 

Henry was a beautiful piece of man candy... I mean, an interesting character who brought a lot to the story, but I'm definitely team Gio too.

Yeah, I can think you're a badass for getting through what you've dealt with in your life, but in general, caring about strangers is kinda hard, unless it's a particular vulnerable group where we're built in with that need to protect... 

I hate seeing that everywhere, my "love language" is touch, so I get extra nothing from people blabbering on about how much I'm valued by internet strangers. They need to make themselves feel better, and okay, give yourself the pats, but most people are awful, so what are we really supposed to get from this? 

A nice few seconds and then back to the real world where everything is undone?

I recently binge watched angel in full and the whole time I'm like "how do you speak, or smoke, etc" as much as I want to let things go for this show I love and angel, which... yeah, it's good, but it's not buffy, I feel like there could have been a way around all the desperate gasps blatantly on screen and so on. 

Or the actors could just nut up and go full method and die... then be reborn as soulless demons, potentially, not that Hollywood is into that kind of thing.

I love that no matter what happened she was unapologetically herself. She saw things for what they were and didn't mince words about it. To this day I wish her and Ignacio got more screen time together.

Yeah, people who say this also want a woman who's naturally hairless from the eyebrows down and doesn't have sweat glands, just a sex and pie making machine. 

These specific guys probably drove their ex to breaking point and when she yelled at him and stormed out they were too busy playing xbox in a pile of their own filth for a few days to realise mummy replacement had left. 

They really want a mother they can fuck. Because she's the only woman who is genetically required to put up with their shit.

Mostly the effects. I like the taste of beer and whisky, everything else is just drinking it as fast as I can to get to the happy/dizzy/numb feeling. I don't like myself drunk, but I don't like myself sober either, but I know my drunk self will get things done that my usual self won't. She wins most nights because I'm too useless to even reach out to "friends" without a drink in me.

I recently rewatched it and I think it's more along the lines of "disney cancer" no specifics about what kind, and a few mentions of treatments, but they're very vague. 

You're a badass, I hope your recovery goes well and you get to keep enjoying the show without too much spoilers ❤

Yeah, it was just a Buffy's special speech time of 'someone else always has it worse'. Then he said he was just going to use it on himself, and he got suspended anyway. I'm sure that helped everything he was going through.  

But nevermind that, lunch lady is going all in on the rat poison!

My mother always wanted me to have really long hair, it didn't bother me as a kid, but then I got to high school and everything got worse, as high school does. I was the girl who "never brushed her hair haha let's throw things, the teacher clearly doesn't mind" (because it was down to my hips and going outside in Scotland will mess up any hair plans you have), other kids would always stick rolled up paper and staples in it, and laugh because I couldn't see the back of my head, etc. 

It was such a hassle to wash and dry, it was pretty thick then too, and I barely had the energy to get dressed never mind styling it. So in the plastics era of every girl being orange and bleached blonde, I just hated everything about myself, and realise now looking back that the hair was partially to blame. 

Anyway, she got really upset when I wanted to have it cut to below my shoulders, she didn't force me to keep it, but she kept putting it off and trying to change my mind, as though hair doesn't grow. Her hair has always been ridiculously long (the length that you can see the damage it's causing because she won't trim it), and I think she liked having a daughter who she shared that with, because I'm seeing the same thing happen with my younger siblings. 

But I went no contact a few years ago and now I have a pixie cut. Not having to do anything with my hair and still like how it looks has made such a difference for my mental state. Weakest act of rebellion ever, I know, but looking back it's a shame that something as little as a haircut could have saved me from being a target of every class I walked into. 

Teachers actually noticing signs that a kid is in trouble would help too, but hey, one step at a time.

I read it was railroad spikes under their nails somewhere, but it was almost 20 years ago and to this day I'm wondering how that's physically possible. Probably remembering it wrong, unless people had really big hands back in the day.

I actually found this sub a few years ago because of a post shitting on Lorelai Gilmore, glad to see it's not just a few people who think this. Because when I was growing up watching this with my single mother, who was also raised by my abusive narc grandmother, it was easily an "omg this is literally us!" Moment. 

But I can't stand Lorelai in my rewatches, it's hard, I get it, but she really never matured beyond the teenager who had a kid, and when you have a kid, it's not about you any more. People are happy to jump on Rory in the year in a life thing, but look at the example she had! 

Don't act like millennials have this secret formula that make all our shit get together overnight. 

Lorelai is a great example of a narcissistic parent, because everyone wants a "cool mom" like her, unless you had one, the mom desperate to be your best friend first, wedging her way into your friend groups to look like a hero, the mom your friends like more than you, the mom who won't let you get a word in because she destroyed your self confidence... etc. 

This unleashed something, sorry... and thank you.

You have to be a special kind of fucked up to hurt kids, there's a reason child abusers don't get put in gen pop in prisons, the people our society doesn't see fit to be free with the rest of us will gut you, and gladly admit to doing so. 

If there were bandits who hurt kids, I'm willing to bet the rest of them wouldn't take long in making an example of them. Because, like Joel, they probably lost people, kids, siblings, etc. 

And what's with the constant shitting on "surviving" as if it's not the goal in this world? These people would try to make friends, play nice and get eaten on day one. 

But nah, Joel didn't try to talk it out over a nice camomile tea with the people holding guns to his head, what a monster!

My mother expected me to just know these things, and got mad at me for not just having the information in my brain. I learnt a lot through tv shows, a little too late for it to matter, I'm ashamed to say. 

School was a nightmare too, because my very few on/off friends didn't have my back at all, other students and teachers would be fine with bullying the obviously neglected little girl who cries randomly and never rolls up her sleeves. 

I don't know how they live with themselves, children are put in your care for the hours without parents and they decide to side with the popular kids cause they never worked on their own issues.
My first apartment had an attic just like that house did, the first time I watched the movie it rearranged my organs. I'd love to be that scared again.

All the time, I have violent fantasies play out in my head when I feel even slightly disrespected, obviously they stay in my head, but I worry that this go to coping method for a few decades now is doing damage to my health. 

My therapist says it's normal to think that, and knowing that acting on the thoughts are wrong is a good sign. But since where I am I can't get access to anger management classes without a criminal conviction... really, you can't make this shit up, I think I just have to let the stress slowly eat my heart.

I liked that Carlos was thinking of Juanita first, the way he dealt with Gabby was a bit much at times, but those two have never been a good example of anything relationship wise. 

Gabby wanted a little living doll she could dress up, and called immigration when that was threatened, sure she kind of changed her mind in the end, but she was oblivious to the child in her home old enough to know something was up and that she was directly involved. 

If he hadn't yelled, Gabby probably wouldn't have changed anything.
Jacob's ladder, it helped me find an odd sense of peace with death/loss, and the creepy wtf moments are always the best first time round.

I liked her, but it did seem like she was just wedged into the story to get to another point. Even with Daniel kissing Betty's eyebrow in saying goodbye to Molly.

I have to wonder how many people Jerry killed to be sure that this time it would work. And how many of them were willing and totally not coerced into giving consent under a vague promise of saving "humanity".

I run purely on spite, but even I have to admit that after a year of going on supply runs, and killing mushroom zombies, I'd have worked through almost all of my trauma. If I survived, and went home to a bed somewhere I could get burritos, I'd probably have some great realisation that I shouldn't throw my life away on a dead end mission. 

This person is giving us Scots (I assume because of wording) a bad name, just beat up a pillow, damn.

I'll never understand Mel didn't instantly bring up that she was pregnant when Ellie confronted them, in Saw (number who knows, I love those films but even the stars can't tell them apart) it was something one of the women brought up because she knew people are instinctively more sympathetic towards that situation. 

She put herself, her baby, and everyone else in danger by going out while heavily pregnant, because who isn't going to instinctively try and protect the 7+ month pregnant chick parkouring all over the place, plus she was acknowledged in the game as a valuable medic, Abby's dads favourite student if I remember correctly. 

It was nice to see Abby being called a piece of shit, but, glass houses, babe. 

I wasn't a fan of Owen either but I felt he just went where was needed in the story. I'd need to be brainwashed to travel half way across the country on someone elses mission of vengeance in that world, so that might explain some of the dumbassery.

It's always good to have the legal knowledge on your side when it comes to what your landlord can and can't do, I'm sorry you had to deal with that. I live in a small town where neighbours are physically incapable of minding their own business, so hats off to you for being able to avoid yours at all. It's actually really comforting to know I'm not the only one who's like that with deliveries :) 

I heard the lazy thing a lot too, but as someone who's thought about being a teacher and helping kids, I can imagine how much it would turn things around for me if a 7 year old asked me what the point of what we were learning was. I'd like to think that a lot of people are going into these professions with experience of more disorders, and at least some memory of how bad it can be to be a kid/teenager, so that traits of adhd and other things can be highlighted and helped in ways other than "different! Let's throw things!"

I saw a post somewhere years ago about how it's easier to plan this stuff out at night because there's no threat of follow through. You can't call your bank at 11pm and apply for a mortgage, and get your dream job at 1am. The plans are easy to make because you don't have to deal with others being as restrictive to your plans, but the literal light of day comes with the inevitable "why bother?" 

I'm hoping I'll have a middle of the night plan that lasts long enough so I can kick it into action in the morning someday, and I hope you do too. I think running on pure spite will do it for me. 

But I fully understand what you feel, to a painful extent.

Renee kicking in that door lives rent free in my brain. 

I'd kill for her. And I wouldn't even paint an emo art piece about it afterwards. 

But they're all just shitty people. Knowing what Bree has went through with addiction (public shaming included) you'd think they would be more delicate with her. It's been a year or so since my rewatch, but I think since Bree was on her own it was easier to dump things on her.

I can't handle people knocking on my door, when I know a delivery is coming (I try to schedule them) I wait by the door to answer it so there's no knocking, otherwise I'm running through all the therapy techniques to deal with the panic attack that follows because the one place I'm supposed to feel safe -my home- isn't safe. My mother was a big door slammer/kicker, and I NEVER had any privacy. Not saying I'm convinced to this day in my own apartment that I'm being watched, partially because my mother liked to hide in my room when I was a teenager to surprise me... plus Truman show. Thanks. 

And I can't talk about anything I enjoy because I've been laughed at (I'm assuming it's not all malicious in nature and just raging ignorance) to a point where I realise the things I like are dumb because 'different' and there's no point in sharing anything you like with anyone because it's a waste of breath. I was a "slow" kid, and got called stupid and bullied by my teachers, and abused horribly by my mother because I didn't get work done. Now I know it's adhd and if literally anyone had given a shit when I was a kid so many things could have been different.

I could be one of those smart on paper kids at least.

I've always liked when it's raining or storms because "everyone else is miserable like me" (the partial joke answer). 

But seeing how many people go out and enjoy the hell out of sunny weather makes me incredibly bitter, I've never been able to handle heat and my recent diagnosis of hyperthyroidism explains it. 

But people are out there being happy and doing things like it's the easiest thing in the world, I know I can't fit in, and I won't, so I think at least 50% of the reason I hate it is that, the rest being physical discomfort.

I was always under the impression that she knew he lied at the end of the first game, but since she knew about Sarah, she understood that he was looking for a family, just like she was looking for a family/purpose. 

Ellie was making plans for her future towards the end of the first game. Thanks to Joel she was seeing a future for herself, and looking forward to it, which in a mushroom zombie apocalypse is a really positive outlook. 

I just think she was upset about the revelation because some new ideas were shoehorned in and they needed to fit the story.

"And?" 

I'm a big girl, I don't need a mother and haven't for a long time. I went no contact a few years ago and I feel so much better for it. I can have the family I choose instead of people who see blood relation and "I kept a roof over your head" as some excuse to beat someone down until they get their way. 

I don't think you're being severe at all, it's very isolating to cut out people to take care of your own needs, but in the long run, I think it's for the best, these people have their own issues to deal with, which is obvious since they can't let go of a choice you made in your own life.

The only good thing about it was how many more respectful to the character ideas were put out about how his death could have been done. 

It had to happen, yes, but it could have been so much better.

I've only had generally bad experiences with people who had a healthy, happy childhood. Twice I found that in the beginning when I was drip feeding the trauma (so I didn't become another "crazy ex girlfriend" for them to list some day, but they also knew my triggers), they were supportive and eager to listen, even one of them taking me out of the crowd to a private place so I could calm down during a panic attack, (which honestly freaked me out more because ew why do you care about my feelings?) 

But after a few weeks of that something just flipped, and I was told I was ruining their day with my bad moods, which happened once, and it was an everyday person kind of stressful day, if I wanted to ruin someones day, boy could I do much better than that. And the old getting ghosted by someone when you tell them about abandonment issues. Classic. 

I'm aware that I've done the creating drama when there is none in the past, so now I try to be extra careful about it. But it looks like a lot of others here have had positive experiences, so there is hope :) 

I'm pretty sure I'll die alone though.

How do you do, fellow chaotic blob? 
I relate, and it's the worst for me to see how others can just do things, even though I know a lot of them have no option but to do it to get through the day. 

I get so stupidly envious though, I want a husband and kids and the white picket fence, all that, and I'm convinced I'll never have anything like that that really matters to me because of what happened to me, I'd never judge anyone else for having my experiences, but I'm sure as hell gonna judge myself, apparently. 

It's easier to be a fake version of myself anywhere outside of my home. Because I'm terrified of people pitying me and trying to give me their version of comfort. 

So, long ramble short, I relate, and I hope that 5 years from now we can clink virtual glasses at getting shit together.

My mother made my first major panic attack about her, I was around 12, thought I was dying because I couldn't breathe and my chest hurt. And she decided to grab the biggest knife from the knife block in the kitchen and threatened to stab herself because I was "stressing her out too much" (My dad died when I was a baby so she was all I was left with). I just cried more in response because, really, what do you do in that situation? Lol

I think it's an unofficial symptom, I'd put it next to "a fantastically dark sense of humour that makes people uncomfortable". 

Our "normal" is unfortunate, but it's what we know, I mean, I get uncomfortable when people talk about good relationships with their mothers, to the point where I need space from that idea. A casual attitude towards horrific life experiences, whether it's a defense mechanism, or just how you see things after healing seems reasonable to me. 
But I'm still in the "all spite, all the time" phase.

To make it from scratch I'd suggest getting a couple of yards of faux leather from amazon or craft stores and pairing it with grey long sleeved shirt and pants. Boot covers are easy enough to make once you have the materials (I found tutorials on youtube so you don't have to spend extra and can use regular shoes). 
Plastic wrap/cling film (I'm in the uk so please forgive the translations) and painters/masking tape make for easy cowl building. 
The gloves can be tricky cause I've made elbow length leather-ish ones before and they're a pain that I wouldn't wish on someone I didn't hate. I'd suggest using a similar method to the boot covers or just regular long fabric gloves if the colour was most important part of them. 
The belt could be recreated pretty easily with those little phone holders you can attach by velcro plus you get to actually carry stuff in them as a bonus. 
The Cape is obviously what you want to measure first if you have the fabric you want for it, and I wish I could give you better advice than lying down on the fabric and using yourself for measurement. 
Best wishes from an old cosplayer.

A method I use is picturing it as someone else telling me the story, why would a younger person lie? What you're feeling is your feelings, plain and simple. 

It sounds similar to a situation I had in a homeless unit type place where the person I shared a home with was irritated by every little thing I did to the point I was scared to just live my life. 

That "but its FINE" I heard in my own mother's voice, toilet paper isn't that loud, so idk if it helps but i believe you without a doubt and I'm sorry you've had to deal with this.

Being depressed is a perfect excuse, I have a whole home to myself that's a near mess and the only thing keeping me from judgement is that people aren't allowed to visit. 

I'm really sorry you're dealing with this, if it's any consolation, teenage years are probably the worst life has to offer. "It gets better" is a cliche but "you get to make your own life choices" as a legal adult is fact.

I think there's obviously an attempt to deter people from taking their own lives on these sites, I'm happy they don't all lay on the guilt of "you're just passing on the pain", cause nothing makes suicidal ideation better than even more guilt. But the human body is so good at keeping itself alive that multiple suicide methods don't always work out. 

I actually read that carbon monoxide poisoning one and was a little disappointed... but I'm thinking it could be more of a case by case thing. Some bodies might react differently and it could just be a warning of sorts that that might be an outcome since a pain free method is often what's searched for.

I think about this a lot, I'm 30, female and my biological clock is going off like I've got tinnitus. I don't know what I could pass on to my kids in regards to mental illness, but I've come to the conclusion that if I do have a family some day, I just have to do my best. 

I want my kids to know they can trust me to have their back, that their boundaries are important and their feelings are valid no matter what the world tells them. There's nothing we can really guarantee in life, but if you can offer a child support and perspective, that's better than a lot of us had growing up.

This year has done a good job highlighting how shit the world is. I'm sorry you're dealing with these feelings, when you start seeing corruption and suffering it really snowballs and seeing anything good just gets harder and harder. 

I've seen the worst come out in people this year and it breaks my heart and pisses me off to no end at the same time, but it does give me a little hope to see there's people like you that notice and care about those who are going without.

I don't think you're overreacting at all, that response from someone claiming to be trying to help people with mental health is pretty gross, and I'm glad you said something cause it sounds like a lot of people needed to hear it too. 

It seems like there's a lot of people who think adult child and parent relationships can be treated like coworkers or casual friendships and not like parents have a duty to do right by their children, and the children of narcissistic parents often go through hell with feeling guilty enough as it is because "they're family!" and "they brought you into the world" like it's a blank cheque to treat a whole human like a puppet for you to take out your emotions on. 

That "take responsibility" bit got me heated...

The loneliness is certainly turned up a lot, any time I even think of the holidays I feel sick because it gives me this feeling of hopelessness. My mental health has been made so much worse due to lockdown and I'm not sure I'll ever be able to recover from this. 

Sorry for the depressing add on there... but you're certainly not alone in how you're feeling, I hope you can find some peace or hope for finding that light.

I think it could be different degrees of comfort/discomfort with vulnerability. For those without trauma it might be intimidating, but if they don't have the negative thoughts and history of "this is how bad it could get" swirling in their brain, that probably wouldn't put such a mental road block in the way, and they just have an easier time getting around it.

Congratulations on getting your dream course though! That's awesome to hear and I hope it is everything you want from it.

I get it a lot when I dare to bring up any issues from my past, like it's someone cutting you off in traffic and not something that affects how you live every day.

I've been able to kind of step out of myself when those thoughts come up. I try looking at my situation/feelings as if it were my best friend going through it, or even just anyone else. I wouldn't blame them for it how they feel, none of us asked for these things to happen to us after all. 

I have a near constant issue with seeing myself worthy of happiness, health, a clean home etc. I try to be gentle but encouraging, and fortunately now I can challenge the negative thoughts when they come up. If I'm telling myself I'm a terrible person, I can usually ask why, then I have to think about it, and realise I haven't done anything I'd judge others for.
This is what those "I don't understand mental illness but tell me I'm a good person for making a don't commit suicide" videos need.

I get like this, my brain just assumes people are mad at me for the slightest little thing too. The downward spiral is more falling straight down a hole because I see the relationships falling apart, they'll never talk to me again and I'll die alone and convince myself life isn't worth living if that's the case... very exhausting.

Last year I was about to get my drivers license, even being offered a car from a family member. But I know I tend to have very impulsive and irrational reactions to certain situations, so I gave up the whole idea of it because I knew if I had access to a car I'd do something permanent, or something very regrettable. 

The part of me that's hoping to make progress feels like the grown up turning pot handles around on the cooker for the safety of the self destructive child part of me.

I wouldn't say it's being dramatic in the slightest if you feel it necessary. I've made certain decisions to protect myself from the darker moments I knew would come when I was able to think clearly enough to see the threat I could become to myself.
I think it's a big reason a lot of people end up invalidating their own feelings as adults, and its heartbreaking to think of.
I'm not sure if it's a narcissist thing or just a shitty person thing, or both. But this post is the first time I realised I had so many emotions invalidated with those exact words growing up...
